7 انخلع It became pulled off, stripped off, taken off, or removed, from its place; it became displaced. (Mgh.) [See also 5.] ―
-b2- Hence, اِنْخَلَعَ قِنَاعُ قَلْبِهِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الفَزَعِ (tropical:) [He became as though] the integument of his heart became pulled off, in consequence of violence of fear, or fright. (Mgh.) And hence also, اِنْخَلَعَ فُؤَادُ الرَّجُلِ (tropical:) [The heart of the man became removed from its place; meaning] the man became frightened. (Mgh.) ―
-b3- [انخلع العُضْوُ, or العَظْمُ, The limb, or the bone, became dislocated. See اِنْخَرَجَ. ―
-b4- انخلع عَنْ عَمَلِهِ (tropical:) He (a ruler, or governor, or the like,) became removed from his office; became deposed. See 1.] ―
-b5- انخلع مِنْ مَالِهِ (tropical:) He became stripped of his property, like as a man is stripped of his garment. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
